correctness.rationale: Parseval applied to |P|² gives 49+2E. Modulating exponents by u+vj multiplies lag k by a single unit phase, and the first two exponents fix a unique gauge without dividing in Z/qZ. Each normalized array therefore accounts for q² arrays even at composite q. Independently computed lag histograms and exact cyclotomic energies exhaust all 29,007 normalized arrays; in the quadratic and cubic fields rational root bounds certify sign comparisons. The replay gives all stated minima and all stated normalized minimizer lists, including just the two conjugate seven-phase vectors, and counts 4,18,16,100,36,98 before normalization. At q=5, 31>13√5; at q=7 the isolating bound for t=2cos(2π/7) gives t>16/13 and hence 19−13t<3. Along with the q=2,3,4,6 energies this proves the first strict improvement. The supplied certificate's Machin bounds, order-41 cosine Taylor remainder (odd coefficient zero), Lipschitz correction and outward rounding are valid; the independent comparison does not rely on that implementation.
residual_risks: The exhaustion is only for seven consecutive frequencies and the six specified alphabets; no continuous-phase or q≥8 optimum is certified.

value.rationale: The length is selected by the canonical binary Barker-seven benchmark rather than an arbitrary sample. The central fact is the exact first alphabet size that improves integrated sidelobe energy, with proof that five smaller alphabets fail and exact equality structure at the transition. This matters even if the numerical gain is modest: a coarser alphabet cannot deliver any gain for this benchmark.
residual_risks: The result is a fixed-length benchmark, not a general phase-resolution law or a claim about peak sidelobe improvements.
